implementation.description: 'native' marks a device implemented as a Rust module in the core. Its commands carry no wire behaviour.

reason.description: Required when implementation is 'native': why the protocol cannot be expressed as data.

label.description: A short name for a person: what a form or button shows ("Channel", "Frequency").

description.description: One plain sentence on what the value means, its unit and numbering, for a person choosing it.

oneOf.description: A step with conditions. when_set: sent only when the named setting is non-empty, decided from configuration before connecting. after_prompt: sent only once the device has sent this text (line-tcp). refused: a reply line matching this regex is the device refusing the credential. accepted: once a reply line matches this regex, refused stops applying.

after_prompt.description: line-tcp only. Literal text the device sends before this step is accepted, such as a password prompt with no line ending. Nothing is sent, and the device is not reported connected, until it arrives; without it within the timeout the connection is dropped and retried.

refused.description: Regex over reply lines. A match is the device refusing the credential: terminal, never retried.

await_reply.description: On a transport whose device replies: queue the step like a query, so its reply is consumed and no command goes ahead of it.

accepted.description: With refused: regex over reply lines. Once a line matches, the device has accepted the login and refused no longer applies.

models.description: The model ids this message is for; it is skipped for any other model (SPEC.md §4, Messages per model).

link.description: With transport.serial: the step is sent only on that link (a login the device asks for on the network only).

codes.description: Device-wide map of numeric response code to failure message, used with expect.code_range.

conversions.description: Named piecewise-linear conversions between a wire value and the value an operator uses (a fader law). Used in templates as {x:to.<name>} (value to wire) and {x:from.<name>} (wire to value), and by expect.convert (SPEC.md §4).

points.description: [wire, value] pairs joined by straight lines; wire strictly rising, value strictly rising or strictly falling. Values outside the points do not convert.

maps.description: Named value tables: a parameter's plain text (an enum value, true or false, a decimal integer) to the wire text, used in templates as {x:map.<name>}. A value the table does not list is rejected before transmission (SPEC.md §4, Value tables).

streams.description: Continuous media a native module publishes, such as a camera's live view, keyed by stream name. Consumers watch a stream by name; frames are delivered outside the event queue, newest only. See SPEC.md, Native modules, Streams.

format.description: The encoding of every frame: jpeg is one complete JPEG image (ITU-T T.81) per frame; meros-preview is one frame of a Meros Camera's preview as the camera frames it (u32 length and i64 pts in microseconds, big-endian, a flags byte whose bit 0 marks a keyframe, then one H.264 or HEVC access unit in Annex-B).

models.description: The models that have the stream; every model when absent.

state.description: Telemetry fields the device reports, keyed by dotted path; '*' stands for a channel number.

telemetry.description: How the device's own messages become state (SPEC.md §8).

every_ms.description: Sent again at this interval (a subscription that expires, or a poll).

poll.description: Queries whose replies go through the rules: one group, or a list of groups each at its own interval (SPEC.md §8).

models.description: The model ids this rule is for; for any other model it is left out (SPEC.md §8, Rules per model).

match.description: Regex over the whole message; captures are {1}, {2}, ...

match_each.description: With match: an RE2-safe regex applied along the rest of the message, after what match matched; the rule matches once per match of it, its captures numbered on after match's and request_match's, and {index} its place from 0. For a list on one line (SPEC.md §8, Lists on one line). With address and match_each_in: applied along that capture's text, for a list inside an OSC string argument (SPEC.md §8, OSC string arguments).

match_each_in.description: With match_each: the capture group of match whose text match_each goes along, instead of the rest of the message (a list between markers, SPEC.md §8, Lists on one line). On an address rule, required: the capture, numbered across the address's and arg_match's, whose text it goes along.

header.description: Regex over a block's first line.

each_line.description: With header: regex applied to every following line; {index} is the line's place among those matching, from 0.

quiet_ms.description: In place of a message selector: the rule's state is assigned once per connection, when the stream (line-tcp, osc-tcp or ws) has been silent this long after the device last sent anything; for a status dump whose end is not marked. At most one such rule, with state only (SPEC.md §8, A status dump that ends in silence).

fields.description: With header: 'name: value' lines to state paths.

address.description: Regex over an OSC address; arguments are {arg0}, {arg1}, ...

json_arg.description: With address and json, json_match or json_each: the string argument holding JSON (default 0).

oneOf.description: Value template over the rule's captures, with the directives of SPEC.md §4 (Formatting directives): {4:bit.3} is true while bit 3 of a flags word is set.

map.description: Wire text to state value; wire values not listed are not assigned.

oneOf.description: Remove the path from state: a declared value, or a whole subtree of declared values (a JSON merge patch null).

state.description: State path template to value, or to {delete: true} to remove it.

path.description: Regex over an HTTP request's path and query; the rule handles its reply.

json.description: With path: names for values taken from a JSON reply, by JSON path. With address: from the JSON in the string argument at json_arg. With json_match alone: from the JSON message.

headers.description: With path: names for response header values, by header name in any case (SPEC.md §8).

xml_each.description: With path: an XML element name; each such element in the reply is a match, its attributes the captures, then {text} its own text, each child element holding only text by the child's name, and the attributes of the elements it lies in as {^name} (one out), {^^name} (two); a name already captured is kept (SPEC.md §8).

json_each.description: With path, json_match or address, and json: a JSON path to an array; the rule matches once per element, json paths relative to it. [*] in the path goes through every element of an array on the way ($.data[*].ingest_streams); $^. names the element one level out, $^^. two, and {index} is the element's index in its array; {^index} and {^key} are the index and member name of the element one level out, {^^index} two. A member name may be {settings.name}, filled in from the settings current when the message arrives (SPEC.md §8).

each_match.description: With json_each: JSON path from each element ($^. for the element one level out) to an RE2-safe regex its value must match, as json_match does for the message; an element that does not match is skipped, values, then_send and replace alike. Its captures are numbered on after the path's and json_match's (SPEC.md §8, Lists).

arg_types.description: With address: the message's OSC type tags must be exactly these (without the comma), for a device that sends different shapes on one address.

arg_match.description: With address: an argument's index to an RE2-safe regex its text must match (a number as its decimal text); its captures are numbered on after the address's, in index order (SPEC.md §8, OSC string arguments).

json_match.description: JSON path to an RE2-safe regex its value must match (a string as is, anything else as compact JSON). Alone: a JSON message on a websocket, an event stream, or a line of a line transport. With path: the JSON reply must match too. With address: the JSON in the string argument at json_arg must match. Captures are {1}, {2}, ... across the regexes in order, after the path's or the address's.

request_match.description: With path: JSON path to an RE2-safe regex the JSON body of the request the reply answers must match, so replies sharing one path (JSON-RPC) can be told apart. Its captures come after the path's and before json_match's. With match, on a line transport: an RE2-safe regex over the text of the message the reply answers (the device answers one message at a time, in order), its captures numbered on after match's (SPEC.md §8, Replies and what they answer).

then_send.description: Messages queued when the rule matches, as poll items are: templates over the rule's captures ({1}, json and headers names) and settings. A message already waiting is not queued again. For a push that only says something changed (SPEC.md §8, Re-reads on a push).

replace.description: State subtrees the rule's values replace: removed whenever the rule's message arrives (its path, header or selectors match, even with no element), before its values are applied, so a list that shrinks or empties leaves nothing behind. Templates over the captures before json_each; with json_each, also rendered for each element from its captures (its json names, {index}, each_match), removing that element's subtree. Alone (no state), beside the plain rule that writes the values, when only some messages hold the whole list (SPEC.md §8, Lists).

websocket.description: A websocket opened beside the transport, for a device that takes commands one way (REST) and pushes state on a websocket. Its messages go through the update rules; it is reopened with backoff when it closes.

url.description: In place of path, port and scheme: an absolute URL on any host, a template over settings rendered (values percent-encoded) at each opening, so a refreshed token in it is the current one. wss, or ws only to this machine. The transport's credential and headers are not sent there (SPEC.md §8).

port.description: Defaults to the transport's port; or {setting: name} naming an integer setting (empty: the transport's port).

scheme.description: ws or wss, or {setting: name} naming an enum setting whose values are ws and wss, or http and https (the REST API's own scheme setting: http opens ws, https wss).

accept_invalid_certs.description: Over wss, accept a certificate that does not chain to a trusted root, such as a device's self-signed one. The connection is encrypted; the device is not authenticated. Defaults to the http transport's accept_invalid_certs.

send.description: Text messages (templates over settings) sent each time the websocket opens: the subscriptions.

every_ms.description: Send the send items again at this interval while the websocket is open: a keepalive the device requires, or a request it answers with state.

socketio.description: The websocket speaks Socket.IO over Engine.IO (path usually /socket.io/): the core adds EIO and transport to the query, joins the namespace when the server opens, answers pings, sends each send item as an event (a JSON array, ["name", data]), and gives each event to the json_match rules as {"event", "data", "args"}.

engine_io.description: 4 for Socket.IO 3 and 4 (the server pings), 3 for Socket.IO 2 (the client pings).

auth.description: A JSON object, a template over settings, sent with the namespace connect as Socket.IO's handshake auth (FreeShow's {"token": ...}).

idle_ms.description: Reopen the websocket when nothing has arrived for this long: for a service that sends keepalives, so silence means a dead connection.

as_reply.description: Each JSON message is also offered to the path rules as the reply to a GET of the path at this JSON path (under prefix), with the value at body as its body, as for telemetry.sse (SPEC.md §8, A push websocket beside the transport).

prefix.description: A fixed path the named path is under (/control/api/v1 for a camera naming /lens/iris).

sse.description: A server-sent event stream opened beside an http transport, with the transport's credential, for a device that pushes changes as text/event-stream. Each event goes to the json_match rules as {"event": name, "data": data} (data parsed where it is JSON) and its data to the text rules; it is reopened with backoff when it closes.

body.description: The request body, a template over settings.

format.description: sse: text/event-stream. json: a chunked JSON stream, one document per part, parts separated by a blank line; each part goes to the rules as the document it is.

as_reply.description: Each part is also offered to the path rules as the reply to a GET of the path at this JSON path, with the value at body as its body (SPEC.md §8, An event stream beside an HTTP transport).

prefix.description: A fixed path the named path is under.

osc.description: OSC feedback beside a stream or HTTP transport: the device sends OSC over UDP to a fixed local port (CasparCG's OSC beside its AMCP line protocol). Each message goes to the address rules; it is never a command's reply. Listened on only while the device is monitored.

extension.description: A native addition to a spec-driven device, for what the format cannot express. Named here so it is never hidden.

ports.description: Every port the integration uses, with its default. Exactly the ports the core really uses: the control port (OpenRequest.port overrides it), and any push, feedback, notification or discovery ports. port null means there is no default and one must be given.

setting.description: The setting that changes this port.

when.description: When it applies, if not always: a setting's value or a model.

scheme.description: tcp (the default) or tls, or {setting: name} naming an enum setting whose values are tcp and tls: the TCP link as it is, or wrapped in TLS 1.2 or later.

tls_port.description: With scheme {setting: name}: the default port when the setting chooses tls (Barco Pulse: 9090, or 9091).

accept_invalid_certs.description: Over tls, accept a certificate that does not chain to a trusted root or does not name the device (a self-signed one): the link is encrypted, the device not authenticated.

reply_framing.description: How a reply is delimited. Defaults to 'block' for framing: block, otherwise 'line'. 'terminated' ends a message at any of reply_terminators, with no line ending needed. 'fenced' takes each line as a message, except the lines between two lines matching reply_fence, which are one. 'json' takes each complete top-level JSON object or array as a message, whatever lies between them (the default for framing: json).

reply_fence.description: With reply_framing: fenced. A regex over a line: such a line opens a block, the next one after its first other line closes it, and the lines between are one message (Turtle AV's status between lines of = signs).

reply_block_header.description: With reply_framing: headed-block. A regex over a reply's first line: such a line opens a block ended by a blank line, in place of a line ending in ':' (CasparCG's AMCP '200 ... OK').

reply_line_header.description: With reply_framing: headed-block. A regex over a reply's first line: such a line is followed by exactly one more line of the same message, whatever it holds (CasparCG's AMCP '201 ... OK' and its line of data).

reply_terminators.description: With reply_framing: terminated. A message runs up to and including the first of these; surrounding spaces and line endings are dropped.

reply_match.description: RE2-safe regex. A message matching it is a command reply; any other message is unsolicited.

error_match.description: RE2-safe regex for the device's error answer, which names nothing it answers (Shure's < REP ERR >): it is taken as the reply of a command waiting with expect.reply_contains.

serial.description: The same protocol on a serial port of the host (RS-232, RS-422, a USB serial adapter), chosen per device by the link setting this block adds with serial_port, baud_rate, data_bits, parity, stop_bits and flow_control; framing, replies, telemetry and commands are shared (SPEC.md §2, The same protocol on a serial port). Each line setting is the vendor's one documented value, or its default and the values it allows.

link.description: The link's default: tcp unless given.

serial_only.description: Models reached only on a serial port: with no link given, they use it, the others tcp.

models.description: The models with the serial port; every model when absent. Link serial is refused for the others.

overrides.description: The transport keys the vendor documents differently on the serial port (STX before each command, no line ending, an ACK byte as the reply): framing, open, close, terminator, reply_framing, reply_terminators, reply_fence, reply_match, error_match and pacing (which replaces the transport's pacing as a whole). A mapping for every model, or a list of them each for the models it names (every model when it names none), laid over the transport in order with link serial only.

models.description: The models this entry is for; every model when absent.
The models this entry is for; every model when absent.

type.description: Text over a serial port of the host (RS-232, RS-422, a USB serial adapter): line-tcp's framings and replies, the port and its line settings coming from the settings serial_port, baud_rate, data_bits, parity, stop_bits and flow_control (SPEC.md §2, line-serial).

reply_framing.description: How a reply is delimited. Defaults to 'block' for framing: block, otherwise 'line'. 'terminated' ends a message at any of reply_terminators, with no line ending needed. 'fenced' takes each line as a message, except the lines between two lines matching reply_fence, which are one. 'json' takes each complete top-level JSON object or array as a message, whatever lies between them (the default for framing: json).

reply_fence.description: With reply_framing: fenced. A regex over a line: such a line opens a block, the next one after its first other line closes it, and the lines between are one message (Turtle AV's status between lines of = signs).

reply_block_header.description: With reply_framing: headed-block. A regex over a reply's first line: such a line opens a block ended by a blank line, in place of a line ending in ':' (CasparCG's AMCP '200 ... OK').

reply_line_header.description: With reply_framing: headed-block. A regex over a reply's first line: such a line is followed by exactly one more line of the same message, whatever it holds (CasparCG's AMCP '201 ... OK' and its line of data).

reply_terminators.description: With reply_framing: terminated. A message runs up to and including the first of these; surrounding spaces and line endings are dropped.

reply_match.description: RE2-safe regex. A message matching it is a command reply; any other message is unsolicited.

error_match.description: RE2-safe regex for the device's error answer, which names nothing it answers (Shure's < REP ERR >): it is taken as the reply of a command waiting with expect.reply_contains.

reply_match.description: RE2-safe regex. A datagram matching it is a command reply; any other is unsolicited.

listen_port.description: Receive on this fixed local port, shared between devices and routed by source address, for devices that send to a configured destination. A port, or {setting: name} naming an integer setting; an empty setting means no fixed port.

https_port.description: With scheme {setting: name}: the default port when the setting chooses https (Magewell: 80, or 443).

scheme.description: http or https, or {setting: name} naming an enum setting whose values are http and https, for devices the operator can switch.

refusal_status.description: HTTP statuses that mean the credential was refused, for devices that use 403 for other errors.

accept_invalid_certs.description: Over HTTPS, accept a certificate that does not chain to a trusted root, such as a device's self-signed one. The connection is encrypted; the device is not authenticated.

refusal_status_body.description: What the body of an answer with one of refusal_status must hold for it to be a refusal of the credential; any other answer with that status fails only its request. For a service answering a refused token and other errors (a missing scope) with the same status, as Twitch does with 401.

json.description: JSON paths to regexes, all of which the body must match.

match.description: A regex over the body text.

refusal_json.description: JSON paths to regexes: an error answer (4xx or 5xx) whose JSON body matches every one is a refusal of the credential too, whatever its status, for a service that names a refused token in its error body (the Graph API's error.code 190 under HTTP 400).

auth.description: The credential sent: a method, or {setting: name} naming an enum setting whose values are methods, for a service taking more than one kind of credential.

headers.description: Headers sent on every request, the push websocket's opening and the event stream: each header name maps to a template over settings ({settings.name}). A header that renders empty is not sent. Authorization, Content-Type and Host are set by the core and may not be named (Twitch's Client-Id: '{settings.client_id}').

auth_header.description: With auth: header, the header the token setting is sent in, as is (mimoLive's X-MimoLive-Password-SHA256). Nothing is sent while the token is empty.

oauth.description: With auth: oauth2, where and how the access_token setting is refreshed with the refresh_token setting (RFC 6749 section 6). The token_url setting, when set, replaces token_url.

token_url.description: The service's token endpoint, an absolute https URL.

refresh_ahead_s.description: Refresh this many seconds before the access token expires (at half its life for a token living shorter than twice this).

client_auth.description: How the client authenticates to the token endpoint: client_id and client_secret (when set) in the form body, or HTTP Basic.

validate.description: A token validation endpoint the service requires the application to call (Twitch: on start and hourly). The core sends the access token there once the device opens and after each refresh, then every every_s while open, whether or not it is monitored. A 401 refreshes the token and validates the new one when there is a refresh token; otherwise, or when the new token is refused too, it is the terminal unauthorized.

url.description: The validation endpoint, an absolute https URL, on any host.

every_s.description: Seconds between validations while the device is open.

scheme.description: The Authorization scheme the access token is sent with (Twitch documents OAuth).

probe.description: Liveness check, any answer meaning reachable: one request, or a list of requests each naming its models, the first for the device's model used.

session.description: A login whose answer carries a session (a cookie or a header) sent back on every later request; renewed when the device says it ended (SPEC.md §2, Sessions).

when_set.description: A setting: the session is used only while it is set (non-empty and not false), for a login the operator can turn off; decided from the current settings.

login.description: The login request (templates over settings), or a list of them each naming its models.

capture.description: What of the login's answer is the session: {cookie: name} the named Set-Cookie, or every one with "*" (the default), sent back as Cookie; {header: name} a response header, sent back in a header of that name; {json: path, header: name} a string at that JSON path of the answer's body, sent back in the header named.

relogin.description: An answer to any request meaning the session ended: the core logs in again and sends that request once more.

refused.description: An answer to the login refusing the credential: terminal, as any refusal.

scheme.description: ws or wss, or {setting: name} naming an enum setting whose values are ws and wss, or http and https (the REST API's own scheme setting: http opens ws, https wss).

accept_invalid_certs.description: Over wss, accept a certificate that does not chain to a trusted root, such as a device's self-signed one. The connection is encrypted; the device is not authenticated.

auth.description: Credential on the opening request, from the username and password, or token, settings. A 401 or 403 answer is terminal, as for http.

reply_match.description: RE2-safe regex. For replies taken in order: a message not matching it is never taken as a reply.

endpoints.description: Other HTTP servers of the same device, on other ports, by name (MediaMTX's playback server on 9996; beside a line transport, a HyperDeck's configuration API on 80). A request item names one with endpoint: it goes to the same host, on that port and scheme; the transport's credential and headers go there unless auth is none, the session never does, and its answers do not decide whether the device is connected (SPEC.md §2, Endpoints).

port.description: The endpoint's port, or {setting: name} naming an int setting. The port given when opening the device does not change it.

scheme.description: http or https, or {setting: name} naming an enum setting of the two; the transport's scheme when absent.

accept_invalid_certs.description: Over https, accept the endpoint's self-signed certificate; the http transport's choice when absent, false beside any other transport.

auth.description: inherit (the default beside an http transport): the transport's credential and headers go with every request to the endpoint; none (the only value beside any other transport): neither does. Or {setting: name} naming an enum setting of the two.

supports.description: Allow-list of command keys. A command absent here MUST be refused for this model.

command.description: 'send' is required for spec-driven devices and forbidden for native ones; tools/validate.py enforces this.

oneOf.description: Ordered sequence; all messages must succeed.

multiline.description: A string that may hold line breaks and other control characters, sent only through the json directive, which escapes them (SPEC.md §4, Templates).

secret.description: A credential (a password the command sets): a consumer masks it, and the core never logs or echoes it (SPEC.md §4, Parameter types).

label.description: A short name for a person: what a form or button shows ("Channel", "Frequency").

description.description: One plain sentence on what the value means, its unit and numbering, for a person choosing it.

models.description: The model ids this message is for; it is skipped for any other model (SPEC.md §4, Messages per model).

reply_address.description: Telemetry poll only: RE2-safe regex over the address the device answers on, for a query answered on another address (ETC Eos: /eos/get/... on /eos/out/get/...).

models.description: The model ids this message is for; it is skipped for any other model (SPEC.md §4, Messages per model).

lineSend.description: Line and websocket transports: a text message sent to some models only (SPEC.md §4, Messages per model).

message.description: The message, a template as a plain string item is.

models.description: The model ids this message is for; it is skipped for any other model.

raw_query.description: Sent verbatim, never re-encoded. For positional CGI arguments.

body.description: The request body: a template, or {binary: name} sending a binary parameter's bytes as they are.

binary.description: A binary parameter of the command.

content_type.description: The body's Content-Type, a template (an enum parameter may choose it).

multipart.description: A multipart/form-data body (RFC 7578), in place of body and content_type: each part a template value or a binary parameter's bytes.

name.description: The form field's name, a template.

binary.description: A binary parameter whose bytes are the part.

filename.description: The file name in the part's Content-Disposition, a template.

headers.description: Headers of this message alone, each name mapped to a template over its parameters and the settings (a file name in Content-Disposition). Not Authorization, Content-Type or Host.

models.description: The model ids this message is for; it is skipped for any other model (SPEC.md §4, Messages per model).

session.description: false: sent without the session of transport.session, and needing none, so it does not log in first (a ping).

endpoint.description: Sent to this endpoint of transport.endpoints (another port of the same host) instead of the transport's port. Not on the probe or the session login (SPEC.md §2, Endpoints).

matches.description: RE2-safe regex; capture group 1 is the returned value.

status.description: The HTTP status the reply must have, or a list of statuses any of which is success.

json_path.description: JSON path into the reply: the HTTP body, or for OSC the string argument at arg.

json_equals.description: JSON path to the value it must hold, in the same JSON as json_path; any other value fails the command.

header.description: HTTP only. A response header whose value is returned (a Location, an ETag); the command fails without it.

code_range.description: Inclusive success range for a leading numeric response code.

code_path.description: JSON path to the reply's numeric status code, used in place of a leading code by code_range and codes (Magewell's $.status).

address.description: OSC only. Templated address the reply must carry; usually /-prefixed, but a device may answer on an address without one (the X32's /node is answered on node).

arg.description: OSC only. Index of the reply argument returned as the value.

reply_json.description: Websocket only. JSON path to a template: the reply is the message whose values at these paths equal the rendered templates (a request id, or the parameter asked for). Without it, the next message is the reply.

reply_contains.description: Line transports only. A template: the reply is the first message holding the rendered text (the parameter and channel asked about); other messages arriving meanwhile are not the reply. Without it, the next message is the reply.

convert.description: The name of a conversion: the returned value is converted from the wire.

replies.description: Line transports only. How many replies each message of the command takes (Quartz's name writes: the name, then an acknowledge); the reply expect checks is all of them, joined by line breaks. Default 1.

models.description: Model ids, or the single entry 'all'.

json.description: JSON paths to RE2-safe regexes the answer's body must all match.

serialByModel.description: Defaults of a serial line setting for the models named, where their factory value is not the block's default (SPEC.md §2, The same protocol on a serial port). Each model is named once, each default is one of the values.

pacing.description: The least time the device needs between the messages it is sent (SPEC.md §2, Pacing). A message that would go too soon is held back with everything behind it, so nothing is reordered; commands, their several messages, polls, subscriptions and on_connect steps are all paced. Requests to an endpoint are not.

min_interval_ms.description: Between any two messages, ms; 0 when absent.

from.description: Where a gap is counted from: the previous message's sending, or its reply (its sending when it awaited none).

by_model.description: Models whose vendor documents another gap.

models.description: The models this entry is for.

groups.description: Messages told apart by their text, by name, each with its own gap.

match.description: An RE2-safe regex on the message as sent without framing: a line message's text, an HTTP request's path and query, a websocket message, an OSC address.

min_interval_ms.description: Between two messages of the group, ms.

after_ms.description: After a message of the group, before any message, ms (a projector's power command).

by_model.description: Models whose vendor documents other values.

models.description: The models this entry is for.
